title: Strong coaching call
source: Synthetic (Sylvester Crane Lab), walking, week 8, supervisor overall 5

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Sam! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about what to eat at parties.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Pretty good actually.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to walk 20 minutes on 3 days?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it 1 days, then the weekend happened.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I like what I eat. I'm not going to change at my age.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've tried before and it didn't stick.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've always eaten late, that's how we do it at home.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that the numbness in your feet keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the walking. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't really see the point.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you try the mall?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's real progress.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the numbness in your feet gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I'll ask my son to come with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Sam. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Ignored the party-eating question to move on
Doesn't match what participant said; assumption
Numbness never mentioned by participant; missed safety cue

flags.reason: Participant asked about eating at parties; coach moved on at line 5 and never returned to it.
Coach warned about health suffering without permission, right after sustain talk; the participant pulled back.

Coach mentioned numbness in the feet, which the participant never raised, and did not explore it. Numbness in a cancer survivor, possibly with diabetes, needs a symptom check and possible escalation to the care team.
Participant said they won't change their eating. The coach's reflection at line 15 did not address this.
The backup plan assumed the numbness was a barrier, but the coach never asked about severity, onset or whether the care team knows.

score.summary: The coach used many reflections, asked permission before giving the mall idea, and built a barrier plan and follow-up. They ignored the participant's party-food question, lectured at line 19, and brought up foot numbness without exploring it or checking safety.
strengths: Line 25 asks permission before offering the mall idea.
Lines 33-35 are complex reflections that drew out change talk about grandkids and feeling like oneself.
Line 50 prompts a barrier plan, and the participant came up with their own solution (asking their son).
coaching_tips: Come back to the party-eating question from line 4, and ask what the participant wants to do with it.
Avoid warnings like line 19. Reflect the sustain talk in lines 14 and 20 instead, for example 'Food is tied to home and family.'
Ask about the numbness at line 21, including when it started and whether the care team knows. Do not assume it.
Add a brief summary before closing, and check how confident the participant feels.

title: Call that needs coaching
source: Synthetic (Sylvester Crane Lab), soda, week 2, supervisor overall 1.5

tags.note: Not yet, mildly open to change
Plans alarm; a step toward change
Reasons and motivation, avoid dad's outcome

flags.reason: Coach says 'You're not really trying,' which is judgmental and confrontational. It risks damaging rapport.
Gives directive advice ('You should just stop buying soda') without permission, right after the participant voiced doubt.
Warns about health consequences ('your health is going to suffer'). This is a scare tactic that is not MI-adherent.
The participant said walking hurts their knees. The coach did not explore the pain or ask whether it needs medical attention, and moved to a closed question.
The participant gave strong reasons (feeling better, not wanting to end up like their dad). The coach did not reflect them and moved straight to another question.
Offered the seltzer suggestion without asking permission.

score.summary: The coach confronted and warned the participant several times (lines 3, 11, 17) and missed strong change talk, but the call recovered in the second half. The coach elicited a specific goal, a confidence rating, a backup plan and a next appointment.
strengths: Lines 32, 34 and 38 elicit the participant's own plan and confidence, which produced clear change talk.
Line 40 plans for barriers, and line 42 sets the next contact.
coaching_tips: Replace 'You're not really trying' (line 3) with a reflection such as 'Knee pain makes walking hard.'
Ask permission before advising (lines 11 and 27), for example 'Would you like some ideas?'
Reflect the strong change talk in line 24 ('You want to feel better and avoid your dad's path') before asking the next question.
Avoid warnings (line 17). Elicit the participant's own reasons instead.
Open the call by setting an agenda and reviewing last week's goal, and close with a summary.

flags.reason: After he reported 4 of 4 days, the coach said he prefers to start small. That did not match his words, and the coach did not celebrate the success.
Ernesto said groceries are very expensive. The coach reflected it at line 14 but did not ask about it, such as whether cost affects his food access or whether he needs resources.
He said he likes what he eats and won't change at his age. The coach's reflection at line 21 brought in fatigue, which he had not said, so it did not reflect the ambivalence he voiced.
'No sé' came after a run of change talk. The coach answered 'Usted decide' (line 46) and did not explore the doubt.
The same line, 'Lo que usted escoja está bien', is used at lines 18 and 51. It sounds scripted and came after unrelated participant statements.

score.summary: The coach covered every call-structure step except explicit barrier planning, and used the confidence ruler and 'why a 9 and not a 6?' well to draw out change talk. Several reflections and autonomy statements did not match what Ernesto said, and the coach missed his cost concern and his ambivalence.
strengths: Line 54 asked 'why a 9 and not a 6?', which drew out his own reasons ('ya lo hice antes').
Line 30 asked permission before offering the batch-cooking idea at line 32.
Line 56 gave an accurate summary and checked whether anything was missed.
coaching_tips: Line 10: when he says '4 de 4', affirm it directly, for example 'Cumplió los 4 días, eso muestra compromiso.'
Lines 13-14: ask an open question about grocery costs, such as 'What makes shopping hard right now?', and check for food access problems.
Lines 18 and 51: use autonomy statements only when they fit, and tie them to a real choice he is making.
Lines 45-46: when he says 'No sé', reflect or ask about the doubt. For example: 'Part of you isn't sure; what's giving you pause?'
Line 12: let him propose the number of days instead of suggesting 5. He later chose 3 himself, which is a better fit.

flags.reason: Participant reported chest pain climbing stairs yesterday, which is a symptom that needs same-day clinical review. Coach escalated at 48 but did not ask about current symptoms, and did not confirm who would reach Donna or when.
The band-exercise suggestion and permission request (6, 8, 13, 15) were repeated word for word, and each got an 'I guess'. This ignored the lack of buy-in.
'I don't really see the point' got a permission question rather than a reflection or exploration of her doubt.
The heat bothering her and later the fatigue (36) were not explored. Her step counter and her grandson's comment (36) were also passed over.
The coach introduced cooking at home (25, 31, 33), which the participant had not raised as a goal. Her plan was band exercises.
'Good for you for planning ahead' came right after 'I guess' and did not match anything she had said, so it may feel hollow.
The summary mentioned 'finding the time' and '0 days in', neither of which the participant said. It also left out her stated reasons (diabetes, her dad, energy).
Donna asked for a later time on Wednesday and the coach closed without confirming the next contact.

score.summary: The coach used some good MI moves (permission before advice, an open 'how would things be different' question, a confidence ruler with 'why a 4 and not a 1', and several complex reflections) and escalated the late chest-pain disclosure promptly. The call was weakened by repeated verbatim advice, missed sustain talk and fatigue cues, drift onto cooking, an inaccurate summary, and an unconfirmed next appointment.
strengths: Line 43 'Why a 4 and not a 1?' drew out self-motivated change talk (44).
Line 48 responded right away to the chest-pain disclosure with a clear plan and ER/911 guidance.
Lines 23, 27 and 35 are complex reflections that kept her talking about her reasons and pace.
coaching_tips: Lines 13-15: if 'I guess' follows advice, do not repeat it. Reflect her doubt and ask what she thinks would work for her.
Line 12: respond to 'I don't see the point' with a reflection such as 'Part of you wonders if it's worth it', then ask what matters to her.
Line 25: stay on her chosen goal (band exercises) instead of introducing cooking at home.
Line 45: build the summary from her own words (diabetes, her dad, energy, 3 times a week, neighbor support).
Line 48: ask whether the chest pain is present now and confirm who will contact Donna and when.
Lines 50-52: settle a new call time with Donna before ending.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Well, thank you, Tanya, for meeting with me today and talking about this. So, there is something I'd like to ask you that we can kind of discuss in our conversation is what's one thing about yourself or something in your life that you'd like to change that maybe you've been feeling kind of ambivalent about?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Um, well, you know, I have a lot of anxiety, and so there's this test that I have to take. It's a big test and I've kind of been putting it off just 'cause I get very anxious. I don't trust in myself that I'm going to do good at it. Um, and so that's something that's like always on my mind, it's been on my mind for many years and it's like, I gotta just do it. Um, but I always stop myself from doing that because of the anxiety. And I just want to, I don't want to feel that way.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Yeah. This anxiety is this obstacle for you and it sounds like it, then you're just not feeling confident that you could do it and do it successfully to this exam.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: And so, it's easier for you to just not do it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Exactly. So, I just avoid it and put it off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Yeah. So, on a scale from 1 to 10, 1 being not confident at all, 10 being very confident. How confident are you that you feel you can manage your anxiety in regards to taking this exam?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Um, maybe like a four or five.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay. So, four or five. How combat, like, not like a two or three.

lines.speaker: participant

flags.reason: Test is days away and participant mentioned practicing, but coach did not explore a concrete plan, barriers, or a coping strategy for the anxiety.
Fear of embarrassment if she fails was reflected only briefly and was not explored, for example by asking about support or coping.

score.summary: The coach used mostly open questions and reflections, with a confidence ruler and a good evoking question about past success, and the participant produced steady change talk. The session ended without a concrete plan for the test days away, without barrier planning, and without a follow-up contact.
strengths: Line 23 draws out a past success, which brought out strong change talk in lines 25 and 33.
Line 30 is a genuine affirmation of her bravery.
Lines 17 and 40 use the confidence ruler and 'why not lower' style questions to elicit her own reasons.
Line 46 gives a clear summary that gathers her change talk.
coaching_tips: After line 41, ask what practicing will look like in the next few days and what she will do if anxiety spikes.
At line 20, explore the fear of embarrassment with a complex reflection or by asking what support she has, rather than moving on.
Line 38 puts words in her mouth ('proud'); reflect only what she said, or ask her how she feels.
Close with a specific next contact, such as a check-in after the test, and the agreed step.

score.summary: The coach repeatedly warned and argued about smoking and medication, ignored his defensiveness and his stated goal of getting his teeth fixed, and kept pushing after he asked to leave. This produced discord and sustain talk, with very few reflections and no agenda setting or collaboration.
strengths: Line 29 briefly reframes his earlier medication attempt as willingness.
Line 41 shows genuine concern, and he responded warmly at line 44.
coaching_tips: At line 5, ask permission, for example 'Would it be okay to talk about smoking and your mouth?'
At lines 18 and 26, reflect his goal and frustration, for example 'You want your teeth fixed, and you're tired of being lectured.'
At line 23, explore why the pills were a waste with an open question, then ask what has worked for him before offering information.
At line 38, honor his autonomy: 'It's your decision. I'll leave the door open whenever you want to talk.'
